verdicts.note: Not the lone-6346 case: nay votes on ESSB 6346, the 2025 package (5813, 5814) and 2021 capital gains (5096) [S6][S7][S8][S9], plus an explicit pamphlet pledge to lower taxes [S1] and repeated statements [S16]. -2/high is supported.

Repeated statements across pamphlet, issues page and interview [S1][S2][S16]. His Ways and Means record includes the McCleary education budget [S3], but the dossier frames it as balanced-budget work, not as a spending-expansion position.

Borderline between -1 and -2: no statement on Israel, Ukraine or a budget figure. But 'a lethal, modern force', rebuilding the defense industrial base [S2] and faulting his opponent for being 'wrong on funding for national defense' [S18] point to pole_a on budget. -2 at medium (not high) already reflects the limited specifics.

His campaign's line that abortion is 'rightly a state issue and not a federal one' [S15] tempers how this plays federally, but the 13-year anti-abortion Senate record, his stated goal of changing WA's law 'someday', and his sex-based women's sports pledge [S2] keep it at -2/high.

The pole_a description ('coalition-building within existing party/donor structures') matches his pamphlet wording [S1]. Contributions from the Emmer Majority Fund, Scalise's Eye of the Tiger PAC and Caterpillar Inc. PAC are confirmed in the cached S17 article. No reform plank either way, so -1/medium and not -2 is right. His 'citizen-legislator ... without becoming part of the D.C. circus' line on the issues page is outsider branding, not a reform position.

0 is a real judgement on mixed evidence, not an omission. Pole_b: nays on H.R. 1 [S5][S6] (Braun calls her 'pro-tax' [S39]), but H.R. 1 also carried the Medicaid changes, so the vote does not cleanly show a tax stance. Pole_a: the family-farm capital gains exemption [S39], and the CTC expansion [S2] is a targeted tax cut. She is publicly silent on the state tax [S39]. Medium confidence is fine because the 0 rests on recorded votes and explicit planks.

High rests on two recorded floor votes (H.R. 6260, H.R. 5214) [S32][S33] plus an explicit platform plank on stricter punishment for drug sale and possession [S2]. -1 rather than -2 because the plank pairs enforcement with treatment, rehab and jobs.

The two sides are not evenly weighted. Pole_b evidence is a belief statement ('real and man-made') plus efficiency rebates for households [S2]; there is no support for carbon pricing or a mandate. Pole_a evidence is three recorded votes with Republicans: disapproving the ACC II waiver and passing the energy-production and LNG bills [S26][S27][S28]. Her own cost-of-living plank also favors 'abundant and cheap energy from traditional and renewable sources' for 'pricing relief' [S2], which is the rubric's affordability-first pole almost word for word. A mild pole_a lean (-1) fits better than 0.

NDAA FY26/FY27 yeas (one of 17 and one of six Democrats) and the Ukraine Support Act [S20][S21][S25] outweigh the Iran War Powers votes [S22][S23], which are pole_b. She voted against the Lebanon War Powers resolution [S24]. -1/high is supported.
+1, not +2, because she voted yea on the Do No Harm in Medicaid Act [S17] (one of four Democrats). Every other recorded vote and statement is pole_b [S2][S12][S13][S14][S15].

Direction is right: she refuses corporate PAC money in the pamphlet [S1], has stock-trading-ban and pay-freeze bills [S1], voted for the Stop Insider Trading Act [S31], and End Citizens United endorses her [S3]. But +2 overstates it. The refusal covers corporate PACs only. The cited S39 article (cached copy checked) reports she took more than $40,000 from the Jeffries Battleground Fund, a party-leadership fund, and $3,000 from the American Sugar Cane League of the USA PAC, an industry trade PAC. The dossier leaves both out. Her issues page says only that she refuses 'special interests (like drug companies)' [S2]. The scorer's note about labor PAC money is not documented in the dossier; only labor endorsements are [S3]. She proposes no term limits, RCV or dark-money ban. A partial PAC refusal plus a stock-trading focus fits +1.

-1 rather than -2 is consistent with Braun's -2: she is a two-term incumbent and appropriator [S1][S4], but her pamphlet runs on outsider framing ('Most members of Congress are millionaires ... out of touch', 'answer to no party') [S1].

missing.basis: His energy plank treats AI data-center power demand as a reason to expand all forms of energy production [S2]. The rubric's pole_a reads 'treat tech/AI growth and its energy demand as opportunity'. That is indirect and he has no AI or platform-regulation statement, so -1 at low.

Pledges to protect Social Security and Medicare [S1] and backed charity-care protections for small and rural hospitals [S3]. That is a fix-the-current-system stance, scored the same way as his opponent's -1. Low because he says nothing on ACA or Medicaid and has no single-payer statement either way.
